intent: A Swedish rooftop and the sky above Africa: the 10-month logger result, the LANDS TO SLEEP plate wiped away for how it naps on the wing, then the bird riding the line to the Congo basin where it spends the winter.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which bird flies the LONGEST without landing?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which bird flies the longest without landing?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: Albatross, Arctic tern, or Common swift?
The common swift. Data loggers on Swedish birds showed some stayed airborne for 10 months straight.

lines.direction: tighten on the Skåne coast; the LANDS TO SLEEP plate waits at the bottom; a mosquito sticker on 'insects', a droplet on 'drink'; on 'nap' the plate wipes away and a sleeping-face sticker pulses as Sweden pulses
lines.text: They eat insects on the wing, drink by skimming water and nap in slow glides high up.

lines.direction: ease back over southern Sweden; a nest sticker and the 2 MONTHS card on 'nest'; a hatching chick on 'fledglings'; Sweden pulses on 'landing'; the Lund pin leaves at the end
lines.text: They touch down for 2 months a year, to nest. Fledglings may fly 2 or 3 years before landing at all.

lines.direction: pull right out so Europe and Africa share the frame; the bird rides the drawn line from Sweden to the Congo basin until 'Congo'; the Congo pin and tag; a rain-cloud sticker on 'rains' as Sweden pulses
lines.text: Each autumn they head south to the Congo basin, chasing the rains and their insects.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Months aloft, never down. Follow us.
